title: fix: TimelineChart reads sgv/mbg fields but measure data uses canonical value field
description: TimelineChart.tsx in kdiab-bff/frontend still reads Nightscout field names from CGM/BGM measure data, so the timeline chart renders no glucose line or BGM dots. Three changes needed in TimelineChart.tsx: (1) line 59: m.data['sgv'] → m.data['value'] for CGM readings, (2) line 75: m.data['mbg'] → m.data['value'] for BGM readings, (3) rename the local mapped property from 'sgv' to 'value' (lines 58, 66, 126 dataKey) and 'bgm' stays consistent. Root cause: same as kdiab-ko5 (backend AnalyticsService) — seed data was normalised from Nightscout field names (sgv, mbg) to the canonical kdiab schema (value/unit/trend) but the frontend chart was not updated. Note: the unit conversion logic (toMgDl using glucoseUnit JWT claim) may also need revisiting — stored values are always mg/dL now so conversion should be based on data.unit rather than user preference.
close_reason: Fixed: data['sgv']→data['value'] for CGM, data['mbg']→data['value'] for BGM, storage unit now from data.unit, Recharts dataKeys updated. Build clean.

title: fix: BFF analytics reads sgv field but measures data uses value
description: The BFF AnalyticsService reads the Nightscout-convention 'sgv' field from CGM measure data (AnalyticsService.kt lines 68 and 111: data["sgv"]?.toString()?.toDoubleOrNull()), but the seed data was updated to store CGM values under the canonical 'value' key. This causes all CGM lookups to return null, making HbA1c, TIR, and AGP compute with zero readings. Test files also build test data with 'sgv' and must be updated.
design:
# OpenSpec: fix BFF analytics sgv→value field name (kdiab-ko5)

## Goal
Fix the BFF AnalyticsService so that HbA1c, TIR, and AGP compute correctly. The root cause is that AnalyticsService reads data["sgv"] (Nightscout convention) but all measure data now uses data["value"] (kdiab canonical schema). Two callsites in production code and three test helper methods use the wrong field name.

## Context

### Root cause
When seed data was normalised from Nightscout conventions (sgv/mbg fields) to the canonical kdiab schema (value/unit/trend), only the frontend MeasureList.tsx was updated. The BFF AnalyticsService still reads the Nightscout field name, causing every CGM lookup to return null and all analytics to silently compute with zero readings.

### Files that need changing

**Production code:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt
  - Line 68  (getAgp):           data["sgv"]  → data["value"]
  - Line 111 (fetchCgmReadings): data["sgv"]  → data["value"]

**Test helpers:**
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt
  - Line 30: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt
  - Line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0); add put("unit", "mg/dL")
- kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt
  - Line 31: put("sgv", sgv)   → put("value", sgv); add put("unit", "mg/dL")

## Interface Changes
No interface changes — the fix is internal to AnalyticsService and test helpers.

## Implementation Plan
1. AnalyticsService.kt line 68:  data["sgv"] → data["value"]
2. AnalyticsService.kt line 111: data["sgv"] → data["value"]
3. AnalyticsServiceTest.kt line 30: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
4. TimelineServiceTest.kt line 29: put("sgv", 120.0) → put("value", 120.0) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
5. MeasuresClientTest.kt line 31: put("sgv", sgv) → put("value", sgv) and add put("unit", "mg/dL")
6. Run ./gradlew :backend:check in kdiab-bff — all existing analytics tests must pass

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest cases now receive non-null cgm values and produce non-zero HbA1c/TIR/AGP results
- [ ] Quality gate: cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check passes (Detekt green, Kover ≥ 80%)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] HbA1c endpoint returns a non-null hba1c value when CGM readings exist in the timeframe
- [ ] TIR breakdown returns non-zero inRangeCount/belowCount/aboveCount when CGM readings exist
- [ ] AGP hourly buckets contain non-zero count values for hours with CGM readings
- [ ] ./gradlew :backend:check passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- The fix is a pure rename — no logic changes, no risk of regressions beyond what tests cover.
- The mmol/L conversion (glucoseUnit JWT claim × 18) may also be wrong now that ALL values are stored in mg/dL regardless of user preference. This is a separate P1 issue and is out of scope for this fix.
close_reason: Fixed: data["sgv"] → data["value"] in AnalyticsService.kt (lines 68, 111) and updated 3 test helpers. Quality gate green.

title: Fix BGM field name mismatch: AddMeasureModal saves value but MeasureList reads mbg
description: AddMeasureModal.tsx saves a BGM reading as {value: 120, unit: 'mg/dL'} but MeasureList.tsx renderDataSummary() reads d.mbg (Nightscout field name). When the field is missing it falls back to JSON.stringify(d), showing raw JSON instead of the formatted glucose value. This means every user-created BGM reading displays incorrectly. Fix: align field name in the modal to use 'mbg' per Nightscout convention, or make the list reader check both 'mbg' and 'value' as fallback.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Fix silent API failure in AddMeasureModal and AddTreatmentModal
description: When a treatment or measure API call fails (network error, 5xx, 401), the modal closes or stays open with no feedback. The user believes the entry was saved. This is a safety risk: a logged bolus that silently failed means the patient's record is missing a critical event and the doctor cannot see it. Fix: show inline error message in the modal with the failure reason and a retry button. On 401, show 'Session expired - please log in again'.
close_reason: Implemented per approved plan. Tests green, builds clean.

title: Add kdiab-nightscout service: Nightscout-compatible API adapter
description: Create a new kdiab-nightscout service (stateless, like BFF) that exposes a Nightscout-compatible REST API (POST /api/v1/entries, POST /api/v1/treatments, GET equivalents) and maps incoming Nightscout-formatted data (sgv/mbg/trend Nightscout field names, Nightscout treatment types) to kdiab's canonical value/unit schema before forwarding to kdiab-measures and kdiab-treatments via their HTTP APIs. This allows Nightscout-compatible CGM devices, pumps, and apps (Loop, AndroidAPS, xDrip+) to push data directly into the kdiab platform without any client-side transformation.

title: Fix token XSS exposure in kdiab-bff tokenProvider.ts
description: kdiab-bff/frontend/src/api/tokenProvider.ts stores the access token in a module-level variable accessible to any code in the JS bundle. If any dependency or injected script runs, it can read the token. Scope the token variable to request callbacks only, or use a secure closure pattern.

title: Add missing security headers to BFF, treatments, measures nginx.conf
description: Only kdiab-profiles nginx.conf has full security headers. The BFF, treatments, and measures frontends are missing X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, Referrer-Policy, and Content-Security-Policy headers. These are required for WCAG and general web security hygiene.

title: Add empty roles validation to JWT Security.kt in all services
description: Security.kt in all four services extracts roles from the JWT but does not validate that at least one valid role (PATIENT, DOCTOR, ADMIN) is present. A token with no roles passes authentication. Add a check that rejects tokens with empty or unrecognised role sets.

title: Fix Keycloak webOrigins wildcard — whitelist specific origins
description: keycloak-realm.json has webOrigins: ['*'] for public clients, allowing any origin. This allows CORS attacks if Keycloak is exposed. Should be replaced with explicit origin list (e.g. http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:3001, http://localhost:3002, http://localhost:3003).

title: Remove hardcoded JDBC URL defaults from application.conf
description: kdiab-profiles and kdiab-treatments application.conf files have hardcoded fallback JDBC URLs (jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/...) that would silently connect to a local DB if DATABASE_URL env var is not set. Production deployments could accidentally use the wrong DB. Remove defaults and require the env var explicitly.

title: Enforce PKCE for all public OIDC clients in Keycloak
description: Public OIDC clients (measures-frontend, profiles-frontend, treatments-frontend, bff-frontend) in keycloak-realm.json should have pkceCodeChallengeMethod set to S256. Without PKCE, authorization code interception attacks are possible.

title: Fix unsafe Record<string,unknown> access in MeasureList and TreatmentList
description: MeasureList.tsx casts measure.data as Record<string,unknown> then accesses d.trend, d.value, d.sgv without type guards. TreatmentList.tsx does the same for d.insulin, d.duration, d.carbs. If a field is missing or has an unexpected type, the code may display undefined or cause a runtime error. Fix: add explicit type guards before each field access (typeof d.trend === 'string'), use optional chaining and nullish coalescing throughout, and consider defining typed payload interfaces per measure/treatment type.

title: Fix Profile status string type in generated API client and remove as-string casts
description: The generated API client types Profile.status as string instead of a string literal union type 'ACTIVE' | 'DRAFT' | 'PROPOSED' | 'ARCHIVED'. This forces developers to write unsafe casts: (p.status as string || '') === 'PROPOSED'. This pattern appears 5+ times in ProfileList.tsx and ProfileHistory.tsx. Fix: update the OpenAPI spec to define ProfileStatus as an enum (not a plain string), regenerate the TypeScript client, and remove all as-string casts to use type-safe comparisons directly.

title: Add status column to kdiab-treatments table and domain model
description: kdiab-treatments has no status field in the treatments table, domain model Treatment.kt, or API schema. kdiab-measures has MeasureStatus (ACTIVE/ARCHIVED) allowing soft-delete via archive. Treatments only support hard delete. Add: (1) Liquibase changeset adding status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'ACTIVE' to treatments table, (2) TreatmentStatus enum (ACTIVE/ARCHIVED) in domain model, (3) archive endpoint updating status to ARCHIVED without deleting the row, (4) update OpenAPI schema and list endpoint to support status filter parameter.

title: Replace alert() with inline form validation errors in all modals
description: AddMeasureModal.tsx uses alert(t('modal.validationError')) when form validation fails. Browser alert() blocks the UI, cannot be styled, and gives no context about which field failed. This is especially jarring on mobile. Fix: remove all alert() calls from form submission handlers. Display validation errors inline: below each field using react-hook-form fieldState.error, and a summary error banner at the top of the form (role='alert') listing all validation failures. Applies to AddMeasureModal, AddTreatmentModal, and any other forms using alert().

title: Fix TIR threshold labels: show mmol/L values when user unit preference is mmol/L
description: TimeInRangeBar.tsx displays zone labels using hardcoded mg/dL thresholds (< 70, 70-180, 180-250, > 250) even when the user's glucose_unit JWT claim is mmol/L. A mmol/L user sees 'Below (< 70)' but their readings are in mmol/L, so the number '70' is meaningless and confusing. Fix: read glucoseUnit from the user context and convert displayed thresholds: 70 mg/dL → 3.9 mmol/L, 180 → 10.0, 250 → 13.9. Pass glucoseUnit as a prop to TimeInRangeBar and convert all threshold labels accordingly.

title: Add prominent patient-viewing banner for doctors in BFF and measures frontends
description: In kdiab-bff and kdiab-measures, doctors can select a patient to view from a dropdown. The selector is a small UI element and there is no prominent indicator that the doctor is viewing another patient's data. A doctor could forget they are viewing patient Sarah's timeline instead of their own. Add a persistent coloured banner (yellow warning bar) below the navigation when viewing another patient's data: 'You are viewing [patient name/ID]'s data — Return to your own.' The banner must remain visible while scrolling.

title: Replace window.confirm() with custom confirmation modals for destructive actions
description: Multiple list components use window.confirm() for archive/delete confirmation (MeasureList, TreatmentList). The profiles frontend uses window.confirm() for accepting a PROPOSED profile change - a critical medical decision. window.confirm() is non-standard, has poor mobile UX, cannot be styled, and provides no context about consequences. Replace all window.confirm() usages with a custom modal component that shows the specific item being affected, the consequences, and labelled action buttons.

title: Fix WCAG 2.1 AA colour-only violations: TIR bar patterns and timeline treatment shapes
description: Two components fail WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criterion 1.4.1 (colour not sole means of conveying information): (1) TimeInRangeBar.tsx uses only CSS colour variables to differentiate 4 TIR zones with no pattern, texture, or text label directly on each bar segment; (2) TimelineChart.tsx renders all treatments as identical scatter points with only colour distinguishing bolus/carbs/corrections. Fix: (1) add text labels or pattern fills to each TIR zone, (2) use distinct shapes (triangle/square/diamond) for different treatment types and add a visible legend.

title: Add full modal accessibility: role=dialog aria-modal Escape key and focus trap
description: AddMeasureModal, AddTreatmentModal, and any other modals in all four frontends lack: role='dialog', aria-modal='true', Escape key handler to close, and focus trapping (keyboard users can tab out of the modal to background content). This violates WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criterion 2.1.2 (no keyboard trap). Fix: add role='dialog' aria-modal='true' aria-labelledby pointing to modal title; add useEffect with keydown listener for Escape; add focus trap using a ref on the first focusable element.

title: Add color-coded glucose zones to MeasureList glucose display
description: In kdiab-measures MeasureList.tsx, glucose values are displayed as plain text (e.g. '120 mg/dL'). A reading of 55 mg/dL (severe hypo) looks identical to 120 mg/dL. Add colour coding by clinical zone: red < 70 mg/dL (hypoglycaemia), green 70-180 mg/dL (target), orange 180-250 mg/dL (elevated), dark red > 250 mg/dL (severe hyper). Also add a visual alert banner at the top of the list if any reading in the visible page is < 70 or > 250.

title: Add proposal reason field for doctor-initiated profile proposals
description: When a doctor creates a PROPOSED profile, there is no field to explain clinical rationale. The patient sees a new profile with no context (e.g. 'reducing overnight basal because of 3am lows'). Without this, accept/reject decisions are made blindly. Add optional proposalReason: String? to the Profile domain model, CreateProfileRequest API schema, DB migration, and display it prominently in the ProfileList PROPOSED section and the accept/reject confirmation dialog.

title: Add edit endpoint and UI for measures and treatments
description: There is no way to edit a logged measure or treatment after creation. Patients make typos (wrong insulin dose, wrong timestamp) and must delete and recreate entries, leaving gaps in the record if they forget. Add PUT /users/{userId}/measures/{measureId} and PUT /users/{userId}/treatments/{treatmentId} endpoints to both services (update data payload and measured/treated timestamp only; userId and type are immutable). Add Edit button in MeasureList/TreatmentList rows that opens the existing Add modal pre-filled with current values.

title: Add CGM trend direction arrows to BFF timeline chart and measures list
description: Glucose trend direction (rising/stable/falling) is critical for treatment decisions but not surfaced in the UI. The seed data and CGM measures include a trend field (Flat/SingleUp/FortyFiveUp/SingleDown etc.) in the JSONB data payload. The timeline chart ignores it entirely. Fix: (1) extract trend from measure data in TimelineChart and render directional arrows at each CGM scatter point, (2) show trend in MeasureList alongside the value. Use standard Nightscout trend names: DoubleUp/SingleUp/FortyFiveUp/Flat/FortyFiveDown/SingleDown/DoubleDown.

title: Add Vitest unit tests for all kdiab-bff frontend components
description: kdiab-bff/frontend/src/__tests__/ is empty (only setup.ts exists). All analytics and timeline components have zero unit test coverage. Create Vitest specs for: HbA1cCard (null hba1c, mg/dL vs mmol/L), TimeInRangeBar (4-zone rendering, zone percentages), AgpChart (24 hourly buckets, empty bucket handling, percentile bands), ProfilesTable (active vs archived display), TimeframePicker (preset buttons, custom range, onChange), TimelineChart (CGM line, BGM scatter, treatment markers, reference lines), TokenProvider (JWT role parsing).

title: Add HYPO_TREATMENT type to kdiab-treatments for emergency carbohydrate correction
description: There is no treatment type for emergency hypoglycemia treatment (fast carbs to treat a low reading). A patient consuming 15g fast-acting glucose cannot log this clinically relevant event. This makes it impossible to correlate low CGM readings with corrective actions. Add treatment type HYPO_TREATMENT with payload {carbs: 15, reason: 'BG < 70'} to the TreatmentType enum, OpenAPI spec, DB migration, and frontend AddTreatmentModal type selector.

title: Add BFF e2e tests for all four API endpoints
description: kdiab-bff/backend/src/e2e-test/kotlin/ is empty. Create Kotest BehaviorSpec e2e tests using the Ktor test engine (testApplication) covering: GET /users/{id}/timeline (auth, access control, date range), GET /users/{id}/analytics/hba1c, GET /users/{id}/analytics/agp, GET /users/{id}/profiles/active. Include JWT generation for PATIENT, DOCTOR (with allowedPatients), and ADMIN roles. Verify 401 without token, 403 for wrong user, 502 when upstream returns error.

title: Add BFF integration tests with mock upstream Ktor servers
description: kdiab-bff/backend/src/integration-test/kotlin/ is empty. There are no tests exercising the BFF with realistic upstream responses. Create integration tests using embedded Ktor mock servers (one per upstream service) that: (1) verify timeline aggregation (measures + treatments merged and filtered by timeframe), (2) verify analytics calculations (HbA1c, AGP, TIR) with known inputs, (3) verify partial upstream failure scenarios (one service down, other returns data). Follow kdiab-profiles integration test patterns.

title: Handle partial upstream failure in BFF TimelineService with supervisorScope
description: TimelineService uses coroutineScope { async { measuresClient } async { treatmentsClient } }. If either upstream throws UpstreamException, the entire timeline request fails even if the other service succeeded. Fix: switch to supervisorScope and wrap each async in runCatching; return a degraded Timeline with the available data and an errors list indicating which service failed. Update the OpenAPI response schema to include an optional errors field.

title: Add safeguard against unbounded memory in MeasuresClient pagination loop
description: MeasuresClient.getMeasures() loops while result.size < totalCount, accumulating all pages in memory. For a user with years of CGM data (e.g. 5 years * 288 readings/day = ~525k measures), this causes OOM. Fix: add a hard cap (e.g. check(totalCount <= 50_000) { 'Too many measures: ' }) or change the BFF to accept from/to date parameters and pass them through to the upstream service to limit the result set before pagination.

title: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to all upstream service calls
description: The BFF correctly generates/extracts X-Correlation-ID from inbound requests (Logging.kt CallId plugin) and binds it to MDC. But MeasuresClient, ProfilesClient, and TreatmentsClient do not forward it in outbound HTTP calls. Distributed tracing is broken: a single user request cannot be linked across BFF + measures + profiles + treatments logs. Fix: pass correlationId parameter to all client methods and add it as a header on every httpClient.get() call.
design:
# OpenSpec: Forward X-Correlation-ID from BFF to upstream services (kdiab-nf3)

## Goal
The BFF extracts `X-Correlation-ID` from every inbound request (via Ktor's `CallId` plugin) and
binds it to SLF4J MDC for local logging — but never forwards it to `MeasuresClient`,
`ProfilesClient`, or `TreatmentsClient`. Distributed tracing is broken: a single user request
cannot be correlated across BFF + measures + profiles + treatments logs. This spec threads the
correlation ID through every layer using the same pattern already used for the `authorization`
header.

## Context

### How authorization is currently forwarded (pattern to replicate)
- `BffRoutes.kt` extracts `Authorization` header into `RequestContext.authorization: String`
- Route handlers pass `authorization` to service methods
- Service methods pass it to client methods
- Client methods set `header(HttpHeaders.Authorization, authorization)` on every HTTP request

### Correlation ID availability
- `Logging.kt` installs `CallId { header("X-Correlation-ID"); generate { UUID.randomUUID() } }`
- Downstream: `call.callId: String?` — always non-null after `generate {}` is configured
- Null-safety: use `call.callId ?: ""` as a safe default (generate always fires in practice)

### Files that need changing

**Inbound:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/inbound/web/BffRoutes.kt`

**Application services:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/TimelineService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/AnalyticsService.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/application/service/ProfilesService.kt`

**Outbound HTTP clients:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/MeasuresClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/ProfilesClient.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/main/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/bff/adapters/outbound/http/TreatmentsClient.kt`

**Tests:**
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/TimelineServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../service/AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/MeasuresClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/ProfilesClientTest.kt`
- `kdiab-bff/backend/src/test/kotlin/.../http/TreatmentsClientTest.kt`

## Interface Changes
No OpenAPI contract changes — `X-Correlation-ID` is a transparent infrastructure header, not part
of the application API.

Function signatures change (internal only):
- `getMeasures(userId, authorization)` → `getMeasures(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getProfiles(userId, authorization)` → `getProfiles(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- `getTreatments(userId, authorization)` → `getTreatments(userId, authorization, correlationId)`
- Same threading through all service methods.

## Implementation Plan

**Step 1** — `BffRoutes.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `RequestContext`; extract via
`call.callId ?: ""` in `extractContext()`; pass to all six service-method call sites:
`timelineService.getTimeline(...)`, `analyticsService.getHba1c(...)`, `analyticsService.getAgp(...)`,
`profilesService.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 2** — `TimelineService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTimeline(...)` signature;
forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)` and `treatmentsClient.getTreatments(...)`.

**Step 3** — `AnalyticsService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getHba1c(...)`, `getAgp(...)`,
and the private `fetchCgmReadings(...)` helper; forward to `measuresClient.getMeasures(...)`.

**Step 4** — `ProfilesService.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; forward to
`profilesClient.getProfiles(...)`.

**Step 5** — `MeasuresClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getMeasures(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to every `httpClient.get()` call (both the loop
iterations in the paginated implementation).

**Step 6** — `ProfilesClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getProfiles(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 7** — `TreatmentsClient.kt`: Add `correlationId: String` to `getTreatments(...)`; add
`header("X-Correlation-ID", correlationId)` to the `httpClient.get()` call.

**Step 8** — `MeasuresClientTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = "test-cid"` to all `getMeasures()`
calls; add a test `getMeasures sends X-Correlation-ID header` that captures request headers with
`MockEngine` and asserts `"X-Correlation-ID" == "test-cid"`.

**Step 9** — `ProfilesClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getProfiles`.

**Step 10** — `TreatmentsClientTest.kt`: Same as Step 8 for `getTreatments`.

**Step 11** — `AnalyticsServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

**Step 12** — `TimelineServiceTest.kt`: Add `correlationId = ""` to all service-method calls.

(Check for `ProfilesServiceTest.kt` — add `correlationId = ""` if it exists.)

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit: new header-forwarding test in each of the three client test files verifies that
  `X-Correlation-ID` with the supplied value is sent on every upstream request
- [ ] Unit: existing AnalyticsServiceTest and TimelineServiceTest compile and pass with updated signatures
- [ ] Quality gate: `cd kdiab-bff && ./gradlew :backend:check` — all tests green, Detekt clean, Kover ≥ 80%

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every outbound HTTP call from BFF to kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments carries
  `X-Correlation-ID` header equal to the value extracted from the inbound request (or a
  generated UUID when the client did not supply one)
- [ ] New unit tests in MeasuresClientTest, ProfilesClientTest, TreatmentsClientTest confirm the
  header is present and correctly valued
- [ ] `./gradlew :backend:check` passes with no regressions

## Risks & Assumptions
- `call.callId` is always non-null after `generate {}` is configured — using `?: ""` as a
  defensive fallback only; in practice the empty string path will never be taken.
- No changes needed to upstream services (measures, profiles, treatments) — they already accept
  `X-Correlation-ID` via their own `Logging.kt` CallId plugin configuration.
- No OpenAPI schema changes, no frontend changes, no DB changes.
close_reason: Implemented per OpenSpec in isolated worktree

title: Add HTTP connect/request/socket timeouts to BFF HttpClient
description: BFF Application.kt instantiates an HttpClient with CIO engine but no timeout configuration. If any upstream service hangs, the BFF request blocks indefinitely, exhausting the Ktor dispatcher thread pool and cascading failure to all concurrent requests. Fix: install HttpTimeout plugin with connectTimeoutMillis=5000, requestTimeoutMillis=10000, socketTimeoutMillis=5000 in the HttpClient block in Application.kt.

title: Add audit logging for doctor access to patient data
description: There is no audit trail when a doctor reads or writes patient data (views timeline, proposes profile, views analytics). This is required for HIPAA/GDPR compliance. Every doctor read/write must log: timestamp, doctorId, patientId, action (viewed-timeline, proposed-profile, viewed-analytics), and IP/user-agent. Store in an immutable audit table. Expose read-only audit log endpoint for admins. Affects all four backend services.

title: Add SerializationException and JsonConvertException handlers to all StatusPages
description: When call.receive<T>() is called on malformed JSON, Ktor throws SerializationException or JsonConvertException. None of the four services' StatusPages plugins catch these. They propagate as unhandled exceptions and return a non-JSON 500 instead of a structured 400 ErrorResponse. Fix: add exception<SerializationException> and exception<JsonConvertException> handlers to all four StatusPages.kt files returning HttpStatusCode.BadRequest with ErrorResponse.

title: Add integration and e2e tests for kdiab-measures backend
description:
kdiab-measures has unit tests but zero integration or e2e tests. The integration-test and e2e-test source sets are registered in Gradle but contain no test files.

What needs to be added:
- ExposedMeasureRepositoryTest covering all repository methods: create, findById, findByUser (with pagination), archive, delete; use H2 in-memory via the same setup as kdiab-profiles integration tests
- MeasureRoutesE2ETest covering: list measures (pagination, status filter), create measure (valid + invalid payload), get by id, archive, delete; verify JWT auth rejection (401) and authorization (403 for wrong user)
- Test data helpers mirroring kdiab-profiles/backend/src/integration-test/kotlin/

Reference: kdiab-profiles/backend/src/integration-test/ and src/e2e-test/ for patterns.

title: Add integration and e2e tests for kdiab-treatments backend
description:
kdiab-treatments has unit tests but zero integration or e2e tests. The integration-test and e2e-test source sets are registered in Gradle but contain no test files.

What needs to be added:
- ExposedTreatmentRepositoryTest covering all repository methods: create, findById, findByUser (with type filter), archive, delete
- TreatmentRoutesE2ETest covering: list treatments (type filtering, date range), create treatment, get by id, archive; verify role-based delete restriction (only DOCTOR and ADMIN may delete); verify JWT auth rejection (401/403)

Reference: kdiab-profiles/backend/src/integration-test/ and src/e2e-test/ for patterns.

title: Replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub base images with GHCR equivalents
description: All four backend Dockerfiles use eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine and eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine from Docker Hub. Unauthenticated Podman/Docker pulls hit the Docker Hub rate limit (429 toomanyrequests), blocking builds. Switch to the same images hosted on GitHub Container Registry which has no pull rate limits.
design:
# OpenSpec: Replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub base images with GHCR equivalents

## Goal
Replace docker.io/library/eclipse-temurin base images in all four backend Dockerfiles with ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk and ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre from GitHub Container Registry, which has no pull rate limits. Also update dependabot.yml so it tracks the new image names.

## Context
All four backend Dockerfiles are structurally identical, using a two-stage build:
- Stage 1 (builder): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited
- Stage 2 (runtime): FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine — pulls from docker.io, rate-limited

Affected files:
- kdiab-measures/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-profiles/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-treatments/backend/Dockerfile
- kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile
- .github/dependabot.yml — has ignore: eclipse-temurin >= 22 in four docker sections; must be updated to new image names

## Interface Changes
No interface changes. Pure infrastructure change.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Verify GHCR Alpine tags exist
Before editing, pull-test the candidate images:
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine
  podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine
If either pull fails, fall back to the Ubuntu-slim tag (:21) for that image.
IMPORTANT: if falling back to Ubuntu image, addgroup -S/adduser -S (BusyBox/Alpine syntax) in the runtime stage must change to groupadd -r/useradd -r -g ktor ktor (GNU/Linux syntax).

### Step 2 — Update all four Dockerfiles
In each Dockerfile make exactly two FROM substitutions:
  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk-alpine AS builder
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine AS builder

  FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine
  → FROM ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine

No other lines change (assuming Alpine tags exist and are confirmed in step 1).

### Step 3 — Update .github/dependabot.yml
The four package-ecosystem: docker entries for backend dirs currently ignore eclipse-temurin. Replace each with the two new image names:
  ignore:
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jdk
      versions: ['>= 22']
    - dependency-name: temurin21-jre
      versions: ['>= 22']

### Step 4 — Smoke-build one image
  cd /home/triplem/projects/kdiab
  BUILDAH_FORMAT=docker podman build -f kdiab-bff/backend/Dockerfile kdiab-bff -t test-bff-backend
Confirm exit code 0 and no rate-limit errors. Clean up: podman rmi test-bff-backend.

### Step 5 — Commit and close issue
Commit message: fix(docker): replace eclipse-temurin Docker Hub images with GHCR equivalents
Then: bd close kdiab-78y

## Test Plan
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine succeeds with no rate-limit error
- [ ] podman pull ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jre:21-alpine succeeds
- [ ] podman build of kdiab-bff backend exits 0
- [ ] No unit tests affected — pure Dockerfile/YAML change

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All four backend Dockerfiles reference ghcr.io/adoptium/* images only
- [ ] podman compose up --build succeeds from a clean-cache state
- [ ] dependabot.yml ignore rules reference the new image names
- [ ] No functional change to the running application

## Risks & Assumptions
- ghcr.io/adoptium/temurin21-jdk:21-alpine may not exist → fall back to :21 (Ubuntu-slim); agent must verify with pull-test first
- If Ubuntu fallback needed: Alpine addgroup -S/adduser -S syntax must change to GNU equivalents
- Adoptium GHCR images are the same JDK build as Docker Hub eclipse-temurin (same upstream source)
close_reason: User rejected GHCR approach before any files were changed. No implementation occurred.

title: kdiab-bff: Backend-for-Frontend with analytics dashboard
description: New kdiab-bff service aggregating measures, treatments, and profiles into a unified analytics frontend. Features: combined CGM+treatment timeline chart, HbA1c/TIR analytics, AGP (ambulatory glucose profile by hour), profiles viewer. Stack: Kotlin/Ktor backend (stateless, HTTP clients to upstream services), React+Recharts frontend. Ports: backend 8083, frontend 3003.
close_reason: kdiab-bff service fully implemented: backend (services, routes, HTTP clients, domain, plugins, Application.kt, Dockerfile) and frontend (App.tsx, Tab nav, TimelineChart, AgpChart, HbA1cCard, TimeInRangeBar, ProfilesTable, i18n, Recharts)

title: feat: expose and display profile active timeframe in analyze dashboard
description: The profile_statuses table stores valid_from (when a profile entered its current status — ACTIVE or ARCHIVED) but this timestamp is never exposed in the profiles API response. The analyze dashboard ProfilesTable therefore cannot show when a profile was active. Fix requires changes across two services: (1) kdiab-profiles: add validFrom field to Profile schema in api/openapi.yaml; join profile_statuses.valid_from in ExposedProfileRepository and map it through the domain model and ProfileMapper to the API response, (2) kdiab-analyze (BFF): extend ProfileDto to include validFrom: String?; update ProfileSummary domain model with validFrom; update the ProfilesTable frontend component to display 'Active since' (for ACTIVE profiles) or 'Archived at' (for ARCHIVED profiles) using the existing formatDate() utility. Fall back gracefully when validFrom is null (older data).

title: refactor: rename kdiab-bff to kdiab-analyze across all layers
description: Rename the kdiab-bff service to kdiab-analyze to better reflect its purpose (analytics dashboard, not a generic BFF). Scope: (1) directory rename kdiab-bff/ → kdiab-analyze/, (2) Kotlin package org.javafreedom.kdiab.bff → org.javafreedom.kdiab.analyze throughout all .kt files, (3) docker-compose.yml: container names, image names, service keys (bff-backend → analyze-backend, bff-frontend → analyze-frontend), (4) root settings.gradle.kts and build.gradle.kts: includeBuild path, (5) .github/workflows: ci-bff-*.yml → ci-analyze-*.yml, release-bff.yml → release-analyze.yml, all internal references, (6) .github/dependabot.yml: directory paths, group names, (7) config/keycloak-realm.json: client ID kdiab-bff-frontend → kdiab-analyze-frontend, (8) CLAUDE.md files and docs/: all references to bff → analyze, (9) frontend: VITE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID env var, package.json name. No functional changes — pure rename.

title: feat: kdiab-calc — insulin dose calculation service
description: Create a new stateless Kotlin/Ktor service kdiab-calc that computes a recommended insulin dose given: current blood glucose (value + unit), CGM trend (direction), target glucose (from active profile or default), insulin-sensitivity factor (ISF from profile), insulin-carb ratio (ICR from profile), active carbs (grams), and duration of action (from profile). The service calls kdiab-profiles to retrieve the user's active profile and returns a structured recommendation with breakdown (correction dose + carb dose + trend adjustment). No database — stateless computation only.

title: feat: show all treatment types in BFF analysis timeline
description: The BFF timeline only surfaces a subset of treatment types. Temp basals (TEMP_BASAL), profile switches (SITE_CHANGE, SENSOR_INSERT, INSULIN_CHANGE), and activity entries (EXERCISE) should all appear as annotated events on the analysis timeline so the clinician and patient can correlate glucose trends with every logged event.

title: feat: add analysis range to profile and wire BFF analytics to use it
description: Add two nullable columns (analysis_low, analysis_high DOUBLE) to the profiles table representing the broader clinical analysis thresholds (typically 70/180 mg/dL) that are distinct from the personal target range (TargetSegment.low/high). These default to 70 and 180 mg/dL (3.9/10 mmol/L) when null. Changes needed: (1) kdiab-profiles Liquibase 001-initial-schema.yaml — add analysis_low and analysis_high nullable columns to the profiles changeSet, treating this as if they were always there (no new migration file, no existing release), (2) Profile domain model — add analysisLow/analysisHigh optional Double fields, (3) OpenAPI spec — add to Profile and CreateProfileRequest schemas, (4) BFF ProfileDto — include analysisLow/analysisHigh, (5) BFF AnalyticsService — replace hardcoded TIR_LOW=70/TIR_HIGH=180 with values from the active profile, falling back to defaults when null. Seed data should also be updated with realistic analysis range values for sarah and mike.

title: Fix outdated port numbers in kdiab-treatments docs/how-to-run.adoc
description: kdiab-treatments/docs/how-to-run.adoc references port numbers from before the root compose was introduced. The service now runs on port 8083 (backend) and 3002 (frontend) in the root compose, but standalone docs still refer to 8080/3000. Audit and correct all port references to match both standalone and root-compose contexts.

title: Create docs/deployment.adoc for production deployment guidance
description: The project has no production deployment documentation. Developers and ops staff have no guidance on: environment variable requirements, secret management, Keycloak production hardening, database backup strategy, container registry, or TLS/HTTPS configuration. Create docs/deployment.adoc covering these topics.

title: Add DCCT formula source comments to AnalyticsService.kt constants
description: AnalyticsService.kt has magic constants (46.7, 28.7, 18.0, 70.0, 180.0, 250.0) used in HbA1c and TIR calculations with no documentation of their source. Add short KDoc comments linking to the DCCT formula origin and clinical TIR guideline thresholds (ADA 2023) so future maintainers understand the clinical basis.

title: Create docs/keycloak-setup.adoc documenting realm configuration
description: The Keycloak configuration is non-trivial (audience mappers, multi-service PKCE, test users, roles). All knowledge is implicit in keycloak-realm.json. Create docs/keycloak-setup.adoc explaining: realm structure, client setup for each service, audience mapper rationale, test account setup, and how to recreate the realm from scratch.

title: Fix port inconsistencies in kdiab-bff/CLAUDE.md
description: kdiab-bff/CLAUDE.md shows PROFILES_URL default as http://localhost:8081 (which is the Keycloak port) and TREATMENTS_URL as http://localhost:8082. Correct ports: measures=8080, profiles=8082, treatments=8083. Also the Swagger URL listed for standalone mode shows :8083 but the standalone bff-backend runs on 8083 (not the same as root compose :8084). Verify and fix all port references.
close_reason: Fixed profilesUrl 8081→8082 and treatmentsUrl 8082→8083 in application.conf, docker-compose.yml, and CLAUDE.md.

title: Create CONTRIBUTING.md with development workflow guide
description: The project has no CONTRIBUTING.md. New contributors have no guidance on: how to set up the dev environment, branching strategy, Conventional Commits format, PR process, running the quality gate before submitting, or the beads issue workflow. Create a root CONTRIBUTING.md covering these topics.

title: Disable Swagger UI in non-dev environments
description: All four services expose Swagger UI at /swagger unconditionally. In staging or production this exposes the full API surface to unauthenticated users. Add a SWAGGER_ENABLED environment variable (default false) to each service's application.conf and conditionally register the Swagger plugin only when it is true. Dev compose files set SWAGGER_ENABLED=true; production deployments omit it.

title: Add rate limiting to all Ktor backend services
description: None of the four Ktor backends implement rate limiting. All endpoints (including login-adjacent JWT-protected routes) are unthrottled. Add per-IP or per-user rate limiting using the ktor-server-rate-limit plugin or a reverse proxy policy to mitigate brute-force and DoS risks.

title: Add InsulinServiceTest to kdiab-profiles backend
description: kdiab-profiles has comprehensive ProfileServiceTest but no InsulinServiceTest. The insulin endpoints (create, list, update, delete per user) have no service-layer unit tests. Create src/test/kotlin/org/javafreedom/kdiab/profiles/application/service/InsulinServiceTest.kt covering: createInsulin (happy path, duplicate name rejection), getInsulins (empty list, populated list), updateInsulin, deleteInsulin. Use MockK for repository. Follow ProfileServiceTest.kt as the template.

title: Add React Query hooks tests to kdiab-profiles frontend
description: kdiab-profiles frontend has component tests but no tests for React Query hooks (useQuery/useMutation patterns). When useActivateProfile mutation succeeds, it should invalidate the profiles query and refetch. When createProfile mutation completes, the returned new profile ID should be used to update local references. Create src/__tests__/hooks/useProfiles.test.ts testing: profiles query fetches data on mount, createProfile mutation invalidates cache, activateProfile updates local ID, error states from API propagate correctly.

title: Pin TypeScript to stable 5.x across all frontend package.json
description: All four frontends declare "typescript": "~6.0.2" which is a pre-release major version. TypeScript 6.0 is a breaking change release that may introduce instability or incompatible compiler behaviour. Unless there is a specific TS 6.0 feature dependency, pin to the current stable LTS: "typescript": "~5.8.3". Run npm install and fix any resulting type errors. This ensures reproducible builds and avoids pre-release instability.

title: Add inline help tooltips for clinical parameters in ProfileEditor
description: ProfileEditor.tsx has fields for Basal rate, ICR (Insulin-to-Carb Ratio), ISF (Insulin Sensitivity Factor), and Targets but no explanations. A patient new to pump therapy does not know what ICR or ISF means or what typical values are. Add a help icon next to each field label that shows a tooltip: Basal: 'Insulin per hour. Typical: 0.2-1.5 U/h'; ICR: 'Grams of carbs one unit of insulin covers. Typical: 1:8 to 1:20'; ISF: 'How much 1 unit lowers your glucose. Typical: 30-80 mg/dL per unit'; Targets: 'Your goal glucose range, usually 80-130 mg/dL'.

title: Add Prometheus metrics endpoint to all four backend services
description: All four build.gradle.kts files include ktor.server.metrics as a dependency but it is never installed in any Application.kt. No /metrics endpoint is exposed. Operators cannot monitor request rates, error rates, response times, or business metrics. Install the Ktor Metrics plugin with a MicrometerRegistry (Prometheus) in each Application.kt. Expose GET /metrics returning Prometheus text format. Add JVM metrics (GC, memory, threads) and Ktor-specific metrics (active requests, response time histograms).

title: Enable strict TypeScript compiler options across all four frontends
description: All four frontend tsconfig.app.json files have several strict options disabled or commented out: noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, verbatimModuleSyntax, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch are all set to false or commented as //true. These are disabled to suppress warnings rather than fix the underlying issues. Enable them one at a time, fix all resulting errors, and commit. Start with noUnusedLocals (safest), then noUnusedParameters, then verbatimModuleSyntax. This improves overall type safety and catches dead code.

title: Add Meal Bolus + Carbs combined quick-entry form
description: Logging a meal requires two separate modal opens: one for BOLUS (insulin units) and one for CARBS (grams). This is the most common T1D workflow (4-6 times per day). The friction discourages logging. Add a 'Meal' quick-entry option in AddTreatmentModal (or a new MealModal) that collects bolus units, carb grams, and a single timestamp in one form and submits two treatment records. Optionally add a third insulin type field for pre-meal correction.

title: Add un-archive functionality for measures and treatments
description: Patients can archive their own measures and treatments but cannot undo this action. Accidental archives leave gaps in the medical record with no recovery path (only doctors/admins can permanently delete). Add POST /users/{userId}/measures/unarchive (with body containing ids[]) and equivalent for treatments. Update the frontend MeasureList and TreatmentList to include an optional 'Show archived' toggle that displays archived entries with an Unarchive button.

title: Add side-by-side diff view when doctor proposes a new profile
description: When a doctor creates a PROPOSED profile, neither the doctor nor the patient can see a clear before/after comparison of what changed. The patient must read two separate profile forms to understand what the doctor is proposing. Add a profile diff view in the PROPOSED section of ProfileList showing: current active profile vs proposed profile side-by-side with changed values highlighted (e.g. basal rate changed from 0.9 to 0.7 at 22:00 highlighted in yellow). This helps patients make informed accept/reject decisions.

title: Add AGP chart explanation text and labelled percentile bands
description: AgpChart.tsx shows 5 overlapping area layers labelled p10-p90 / p25-p75 / Median in a legend but provides no explanation of what AGP means or how to use it. Most T1D patients without clinical training will not understand percentile bands. Add: (1) a collapsed help section explaining 'AGP overlays your readings by hour of day - the narrow band shows your typical range, the wide band shows outliers', (2) direct labels on each band (e.g. '90th percentile' as text on the chart), (3) X-axis label showing '0h–23h (local time)'.

title: Add export/print functionality for BFF analytics view
description: The BFF analytics view (HbA1c card, TIR bar, AGP chart, profiles table) cannot be exported or printed for clinical appointments. Doctors cannot attach it to patient notes. Add an 'Export PDF' or 'Print' button to AnalyticsView.tsx that renders the current view (selected timeframe) as a printable layout including: patient identifier, date range, HbA1c estimate with mean glucose, TIR breakdown, AGP chart, active profiles list. Use window.print() with a print-specific CSS class to hide navigation, or a PDF library like jsPDF.

title: Overlay profile change events on BFF analytics charts
description: The BFF analytics view (HbA1c, TIR, AGP) has no indication of when the patient's insulin pump profile changed. A doctor cannot correlate a TIR improvement with a profile change they proposed. Now that profiles will expose activatedAt timestamps (separate issue), overlay vertical markers on the TIR bar chart and AGP chart showing profile changes. Show a vertical line labelled 'Profile changed' at the date of each activation. This requires the BFF to fetch profile history and include change events in the analytics response.

title: Fix HttpClient not closed on BFF shutdown
description: BFF Application.kt creates an HttpClient(CIO) at startup but never closes it on application shutdown. When the Ktor application stops (SIGTERM in container), CIO connection pool is not drained. Fix: subscribe to the ApplicationStopping monitor event and call httpClient.close(): environment.monitor.subscribe(ApplicationStopping) { httpClient.close() }. This ensures clean connection teardown during rolling deployments and avoids connection pool leaks in repeated test runs.

title: Fix AGP empty-bucket percentiles: return null instead of 0.0 when no readings
description: AnalyticsService.getAgp() returns AgpHourlyData(p10=0.0, p25=0.0, ..., count=0) for hours with no CGM readings. This is ambiguous: 0.0 is a valid glucose reading (severe hypoglycaemia below detectable range). The frontend cannot distinguish 'no data at 3am' from 'median glucose at 3am is 0 mg/dL'. Fix: change AgpHourlyData percentile fields to Double? (nullable) and return null for empty buckets. Update the OpenAPI schema and frontend AgpChart to treat null as 'no data' (render gap in the chart).

title: Add TIR zone clinical explanations to TimeInRangeBar
description: TimeInRangeBar.tsx shows 4 coloured zones (Below/In Range/Above/High) but no clinical context. A patient does not know that 'Below < 70' means hypoglycaemia risk or that the TIR target is > 70% in range. Add: (1) a help section below the bar explaining each zone and the clinical target, (2) aria-describedby attributes on each zone segment linking to the explanation for screen readers, (3) a 'Your TIR goal: > 70% in range' indicator with colour coding (green if met, orange if not).

title: Fix N+1 query in ProfileService.assertUniqueNameForUser
description: ProfileService.assertUniqueNameForUser() calls profileRepository.findAllByUserId(userId) to load all profiles, then filters in memory with .any { it.name == name }. For a user with many profiles this loads all of them from the database. Add a repository method existsByUserIdAndName(userId, name, excludeId) that executes a SQL EXISTS query instead. This changes the N+1 scan (all profiles) to a single O(1) indexed lookup.

title: Validate BFF date-range params: from must precede to and both must be valid ISO-8601
description: BffRoutes.kt requireParam() only checks that from and to exist (not null). It does not validate that they are valid ISO-8601 Instant strings or that from < to. If from is an invalid string, Instant.parse() in TimelineService throws DateTimeParseException which becomes an unhandled 500. If from > to, all services return empty results with no error. Fix: parse both params in BffRoutes with runCatching and throw BusinessValidationException on parse failure or when from >= to.

title: Remove plaintext secret defaults from docker-compose.yml and add .env.example
description: docker-compose.yml has hardcoded fallback defaults: POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-password and KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin. If a developer runs docker compose up without a .env file, the database runs with a known weak password. Remove all :-default fallbacks from secret variables. Create .env.example at repo root with placeholder values (POSTGRES_PASSWORD=changeme). Add .env to .gitignore. Document: 'cp .env.example .env and set real values before first run' in how-to-run.adoc.

title: Add readiness probe /readyz endpoint separate from liveness /healthz
description: All services expose /healthz for liveness (is the process running?). There is no separate readiness probe (is the service ready to accept traffic?). A service can be alive but not ready (database connection pool not initialised, JWKS not fetched yet). The docker-compose depends_on should use condition: service_healthy on the readiness probe. Add a /readyz endpoint to all four backends that checks: (1) database connection can be obtained from the pool, (2) returns 200 if ready, 503 if not. Update docker-compose depends_on conditions.

title: Add resource limits (memory, CPU) to all services in docker-compose.yml
description: No service in docker-compose.yml has deploy.resources.limits configured. A single runaway service can OOM-kill the host. Add deploy.resources.limits.memory and cpus to every service. Recommended: backend services 512M / 1.0 CPU each; bff-backend 256M / 0.5 CPU; postgres 1G / 2.0 CPU; keycloak 512M / 1.0 CPU; frontend nginx services 64M / 0.25 CPU. Also add reservations at half the limits. This is a prerequisite for Kubernetes deployment.

title: Add composite indexes (user_id, timestamp) to measures and treatments tables
description: The measures and treatments tables have separate indexes on user_id, type, and measured_at/treated_at individually. All list queries filter by (user_id, date range) but no composite index exists for this pattern. For a user with years of CGM data, the query must scan all user rows and then filter by date. Add Liquibase changesets creating: INDEX idx_measures_user_time ON measures(user_id, measured_at DESC) and INDEX idx_treatments_user_time ON treatments(user_id, treated_at DESC). Mark with dbms: postgresql.

title: Add from/to date filter params to measures and treatments list endpoints
description: The BFF TimelineService fetches ALL measures and ALL treatments for a user and filters in memory by timeframe. For a user with years of data this is slow and wastes bandwidth. The measures and treatments list endpoints do not support from/to query parameters. Add optional from and to ISO-8601 query parameters to GET /users/{userId}/measures and GET /users/{userId}/treatments. Apply as WHERE measured_at BETWEEN from AND to in Exposed queries. Update OpenAPI specs. The BFF should then pass its from/to params through to both services.

title: Add HbA1c medical context with colour-coded interpretation to HbA1cCard
description: HbA1cCard.tsx displays a raw percentage (e.g. '7.2%') with no explanation. Most patients do not know whether 7.2% is good or bad. Add: (1) a colour-coded zone indicator (green < 7%, yellow 7-8.5%, orange 8.5-10%, red > 10%), (2) a short label per zone ('Excellent control' / 'Good control' / 'Room for improvement' / 'High risk'), (3) a collapsed help section explaining the DCCT formula is estimated, not measured, and the ADA target is < 7% for most adults.

title: Add profile activation timestamps to kdiab-profiles API
description: Profile domain model and API responses include only createdAt. There is no activatedAt or archivedAt timestamp. The BFF ProfilesService already notes this limitation (comment: 'kdiab-profiles API does not expose activatedAt/archivedAt'). Without these, it is impossible to correlate profile changes with analytics improvements. Add activatedAt and archivedAt fields to the Profile domain model, DB migration, and OpenAPI schema. Populate them when status transitions occur in ProfileService.

title: Fix CSS: replace all hardcoded colors with CSS variables, fix dark-theme contrast
description: All 4 service frontends have ~70 hardcoded hex/rgba color values in inline styles that bypass the CSS design token system. Several are light-theme values (e.g. #fafafa, #e0e0e0, #111, #444) that are unreadable against the dark #0b1120 background. Fix: extend index.css with missing tokens (overlay, modal, error, table, badge, code-block), then replace every hardcoded inline color in .tsx files with CSS variable references.
close_reason: All hardcoded color values replaced with CSS custom properties across all 4 frontend apps. 27 files changed.

title: Add Keycloak login theme matching the dark app design
description: The realm config references loginTheme: kdiab but no theme files exist. Users see the default white Keycloak login page, then land in the dark glassmorphism app — a jarring UX break. Implement a custom Keycloak FreeMarker theme under config/keycloak-theme/kdiab/login/ with dark background (#0b1120), glassmorphism card, cyan accent (#38bdf8), Inter font. Update the Keycloak Dockerfile to copy the theme in and set it as the login theme in keycloak-realm.json.
close_reason: Keycloak dark theme active across all services. loginTheme added to root and bff realm configs, theme files created for bff, docker-compose mount added.

title: add ACTIVITY treatment type with name, duration, intensity
description: Add a new TreatmentType ACTIVITY for physical activity tracking. Fields: name (string, e.g. 'running', 'jogging'), duration (minutes, integer), intensity (enum: low/moderate/high). Changes span: kdiab-treatments/api/openapi.yaml, backend domain model TreatmentType enum, Liquibase migration (if needed for DB constraint), frontend form in TreatmentForm.tsx, i18n labels, and seed data.

title: add pagination to measures list
description: The measures list fetches all records at once causing long load times. Add server-side pagination: extend GET /users/{userId}/measures in openapi.yaml with page/size query params, implement in backend route + service, update frontend MeasureList.tsx to use paginated queries with infinite scroll or page controls.

title: fix seed data: use Kohlenhydrate instead of BEhandlung
description: The pg-seed treatment entries contain German label 'BEhandlung' (or it appears in treatment notes/type labels). Replace with the correct German term 'Kohlenhydrate' for CARBS entries. Investigate config/postgres/02-seed-data.sql and kdiab-treatments frontend i18n.

title: feat: configurable page size selector in measures frontend (5/20/50/100)
description: Add a page size dropdown to the measures list frontend so users can choose how many items to display per page. Options: 5, 20, 50, 100. The selected page size replaces the current hardcoded PAGE_SIZE=50 constant in MeasureList.tsx and is forwarded to the backend listMeasures API call. When the page size changes, reset to page 0 and reload. The selector should be positioned near the list title, using the existing .btn / select styling patterns.

title: feat: add cross-service navigation links to BFF analysis UI
description: The BFF analytics dashboard has no navigation to the individual services. Add contextual links from the analysis view to kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, and kdiab-profiles so users can quickly drill into raw data. Links should be relative-URL-configurable via VITE_ env vars to support different deployment topologies.

title: Update build.sh header comment to clarify Gradle-first workflow
description: Since ADR-003 introduced the root Gradle composite build, build.sh is now only needed for Docker-specific workflows. The file header comment still presents build.sh as the primary build tool. Update the comment to clarify that ./gradlew is now the preferred tool for build and test, and build.sh is retained for --docker and cleanup only.

title: Add service ADR indexes to each service docs/index.adoc
description: The root docs/index.adoc links to ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003. Each service (measures, profiles, treatments, bff) may have its own ADR directory but they are not linked from an index. Audit each service's docs/ directory and add ADR links to each service's docs/index.adoc, and add a cross-reference from the root index.

title: Create docs/glossary.adoc with T1D clinical terms
description: The platform uses clinical terminology (CGM, BGM, TIR, AGP, HbA1c, DCCT, bolus, basal, carb ratio, ISF) without a glossary. Non-clinical developers contributing to the codebase have no reference. Create docs/glossary.adoc with definitions and add a link from docs/index.adoc.

title: Create SECURITY.md with vulnerability disclosure policy
description: The project has no SECURITY.md. GitHub displays this file prominently. Add a minimal policy covering: how to report security vulnerabilities (email or private issue), response time expectation, and what is in scope. This is especially important for a health data platform.

title: Replace java.time.Instant with kotlinx.datetime.Instant in BFF AnalyticsService
description: AnalyticsService.kt imports java.time.Instant (line ~8) while the rest of the domain layer uses kotlinx.datetime.Instant per the project convention (documented in CLAUDE.md: 'Use kotlin.uuid.Uuid and kotlinx.datetime.Instant/LocalTime in domain code. Avoid java.time.* in domain/'). Replace the java.time.Instant import with kotlinx.datetime.Instant. Update any comparison logic to use Kotlin datetime methods. This aligns with the architecture convention and avoids mixing datetime libraries.

title: Add healthz filter to CallLogging to suppress health check noise
description: All services use Ktor's CallLogging plugin at INFO level, which logs every request including frequent health checks from docker-compose (every 10 seconds per service). This fills logs with noise. Add a filter to each service's CallLogging installation: filter { call -> !call.request.path().endsWith('/healthz') && !call.request.path().endsWith('/readyz') }. This preserves meaningful request logging while suppressing health check polling.

title: Add upstream request latency logging to BFF HTTP clients
description: MeasuresClient, ProfilesClient, and TreatmentsClient log 'Fetching...' and 'Fetched...' at debug level but do not measure or log round-trip time. If a service is slow (5s response) operators cannot detect it from logs. Add timing around each httpClient.get() call: val start = System.currentTimeMillis(); val response = ...; val ms = System.currentTimeMillis() - start; logger.info { 'Fetched N items from measures in ms' }. Also log HTTP status code on non-success responses.

title: Add Liquibase rollback definitions to all changesets
description: All Liquibase changesets across kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, and kdiab-treatments lack rollback elements. If a deployment fails mid-migration, Liquibase cannot automatically roll back to the previous schema version. Add explicit rollback blocks to all existing changesets: createTable → rollback dropTable; createIndex → rollback dropIndex; addColumn → rollback dropColumn. New changesets must always include a rollback block going forward.

title: Configure structured JSON logging via logback-contrib for all services
description: All services log in plain text (SLF4J → logback default format). Log aggregation systems (ELK, Splunk, Datadog) cannot reliably parse plain text. Add logback-contrib and jackson-databind to each service's test/runtime dependencies. Create a logback.xml configuration (or update existing) that uses JsonLayout for the console appender in production profiles. Retain human-readable output in development. Ensure correlation IDs, user IDs (as MDC keys), and HTTP status codes appear as structured JSON fields.

title: Add profile state machine visualization as chronological status badge chain
description: ProfileList.tsx and ProfileHistory.tsx show profiles as cards with status badges but no visual representation of the state machine transitions over time. A patient cannot see at a glance that Profile A was ACTIVE then ARCHIVED when Profile B became ACTIVE. Add a chronological timeline view (optional tab or toggle) showing profiles in order with dated transitions: DRAFT (Jan 1) → ACTIVE (Jan 5) → ARCHIVED (Feb 1) with connecting arrows. Use CSS flexbox and the activatedAt/archivedAt timestamps once those are added to the API.

title: Create root README.md aggregating common information from service READMEs
description:
Currently only kdiab-profiles has a README.md (startup guide, prerequisites, test users, URLs, production env vars). The other three services have none. The frontend boilerplate README (kdiab-profiles/frontend/README.md) is a generic Vite template with no project-specific content.

Goal: create a single root README.md that serves as the entry point for the monorepo, aggregating all information that is common across services. Trim or remove per-service READMEs to eliminate duplication.

## What belongs in the root README.md

- Project overview: what kdiab is, the four services and their roles
- Prerequisites: JDK 21, Node.js LTS + npm, Docker or Podman with compose plugin
- Quick start: ./gradlew build (primary), docker compose up --build (full stack)
- Build commands table: ./gradlew build / check / clean vs build.sh --docker / --clean
- Service URLs table (full platform via root compose + per-service standalone URLs)
- Test accounts table (sarah/mike/dr_house/dr_cameron/admin with roles and passwords)
- Production configuration: KEYCLOAK_URL and BACKEND_URL env vars (apply to all frontend containers)
- Links to detailed docs: docs/how-to-run.adoc, docs/architecture.adoc, docs/adr/

## What to do with existing READMEs

kdiab-profiles/README.md: replace with a short service-specific README that covers only:
- What this service does (profile state machine, copy-on-write, doctor-patient collaboration)
- The PostgreSQL partial index requirement (IDX_PROFILES_USER_ACTIVE — not reproducible in H2)
- Link back to root README for build, run, and test instructions

kdiab-profiles/frontend/README.md: delete — it is a generic Vite boilerplate with no project-specific content; developers should refer to the root README and CLAUDE.md instead.

kdiab-measures, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-bff: no README exists today; do not create per-service READMEs (the root README plus CLAUDE.md files are sufficient).

## Acceptance criteria
- Root README.md exists and renders cleanly on GitHub/Gitea
- All content currently in kdiab-profiles/README.md that is common (prerequisites, quick start, URLs, test users, production config) is in the root README
- kdiab-profiles/README.md retains only service-specific content (profile state machine note, PostgreSQL partial index note, link to root)
- kdiab-profiles/frontend/README.md is deleted
- No factual duplication between root README and any service README

title: Add root Gradle project for monorepo builds
description: Replace build.sh with a proper Gradle composite build at the repo root so that a single './gradlew build' (or check/clean) drives all four services — backend Gradle + frontend npm — with parallel execution and IDE support.
design:
## Goal
Replace the proprietary build.sh with a root-level Gradle composite build that calls each service's backend (Gradle) and frontend (npm) builds through standard Gradle tasks.

## Context
- Four services: kdiab-measures, kdiab-profiles, kdiab-treatments, kdiab-bff
- All services already use Gradle 9.4.1 with their own settings.gradle.kts and version catalogs
- Each service's root build.gradle.kts currently only has the asciidoctor docs plugin
- No root-level Gradle project exists today
- build.sh handles parallel Gradle + npm builds via shell background processes

## Approach: Gradle Composite Builds
Each service stays an independent Gradle project (own settings.gradle.kts, version catalog, wrapper). Root uses includeBuild() to compose them. Services still build standalone via their own ./gradlew; root ./gradlew delegates to all four.

## Files to Create

### Root level (/home/triplem/projects/kdiab/)
- settings.gradle.kts — includeBuild for each of the four services
- build.gradle.kts — aggregate tasks: build, check, clean, buildDocker
- gradlew + gradle/wrapper/* — copied from any service (all use Gradle 9.4.1)
- gradle.properties — org.gradle.parallel=true, org.gradle.caching=true

### Root settings.gradle.kts
```kotlin
rootProject.name = "kdiab"
includeBuild("kdiab-measures")
includeBuild("kdiab-profiles")
includeBuild("kdiab-treatments")
includeBuild("kdiab-bff")
```

### Root build.gradle.kts
```kotlin
tasks.register("build") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-profiles").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-treatments").task(":buildAll"),
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-bff").task(":buildAll"),
    )
}
tasks.register("check") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":checkAll"),
        ...
    )
}
tasks.register("clean") {
    dependsOn(
        gradle.includedBuild("kdiab-measures").task(":cleanAll"),
        ...
    )
}
```

## Files to Modify

### Each service's root build.gradle.kts (kdiab-*/build.gradle.kts)
Add frontend and aggregate tasks:
```kotlin
tasks.register<Exec>("buildFrontend") {
    workingDir = file("frontend")
    commandLine("bash", "-c", "npm ci --silent && npm run build")
    inputs.dir("frontend/src")
    inputs.file("frontend/package-lock.json")
    outputs.dir("frontend/dist")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("checkFrontend") {
    workingDir = file("frontend")
    commandLine("bash", "-c", "npm ci --silent && npm run lint && npm run test")
}

tasks.register("buildAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:build", "buildFrontend")
}

tasks.register("checkAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:check", "checkFrontend")
}

tasks.register("cleanAll") {
    dependsOn(":backend:clean")
    doLast {
        delete("frontend/dist")
    }
}
```

## Root Task Mapping
| ./gradlew command         | What runs                                    |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| build                     | buildAll in all four services (parallel)     |
| check                     | checkAll in all four services                |
| clean                     | cleanAll in each service                     |

## What Stays in build.sh
The --clean Docker/volume teardown and --docker image build stay in build.sh. Alternatively buildDocker can be added as an exec task in root build.gradle.kts that calls 'docker compose build'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- ./gradlew build from repo root compiles all 4 backends and builds all 4 frontends
- ./gradlew check from repo root runs all tests, detekt, kover, and frontend lint/test for all services
- ./gradlew clean removes all build outputs
- Each service still builds independently via its own ./gradlew
- Parallel flag (./gradlew build --parallel) speeds up builds as build.sh --no-parallel does
- IDE (IntelliJ) can import the root project and see all four services as modules

## Risks
- npm wrapped in Exec tasks has no Gradle incremental support unless inputs/outputs are declared carefully
- Composite build task references (gradle.includedBuild().task()) cannot be used in dependsOn inside included builds themselves — only at root level
- If services diverge to different Gradle versions in future, root wrapper version needs updating
close_reason: Implemented: root settings.gradle.kts (includeBuild for all 4 services), root build.gradle.kts (build/check/clean tasks with group/description), gradle.properties, Gradle wrapper, and buildAll/checkAll/cleanAll aggregate tasks in each service's root build.gradle.kts.
